# Appendix — the legislation and judgments schedule

*Generated 2026-09-11 16:30 UTC. Read-only: no model was
called and nothing was written.*

Per measure: every provision that refers to the instrument the measure names, and every judgment
the research found bearing on it.

⚠⚠ **Whose naming.** Five instruments (M-01, M-02, M-03, M-07, M-11) are the enactment DAVID names, in
his own words (B18 §4). The other ten links, across seven measures, are the enactment **the build's
drafted kernel names** — Lex's reading of his words, not his words — written by `b23-link-instruments.ts`
on 11 September 2026 with that provenance in every row. Each measure prints which it is, and for the
seven, how far the draft *targets* the Act as against naming it as the framework it works within.
Two of the seven (M-05, M-10) are the second kind: the draft's own instrument is a new Bill or grant
conditions, and the linked Act is the law it would operate around, not the law it would change.

## ⚠ What this schedule could not see

Imported from the reference layer's own coverage statement rather than restated:

```
This covers caselaw, statutory instruments (the regulations made under Acts), Acts of Parliament and other instruments. We hold amends, repeals, commences or modifies, from TNA’s own effects data — but not in this search, so they are not joined into any number here. We do not hold this at all yet: a treaty article bearing on a domestic provision. There will be further references we cannot see. A repeal or an amendment is not a citation and is not returned by this query. A change may be prevented by an international obligation this graph cannot see. 25.4% of the references we hold sit in a title, long title, preamble or explanatory note rather than inside a provision — real references, but not provisions that would break. 7.4% point at an instrument we hold no text for, so we can count them and cannot show you what they say. 77 of the Acts referred to here are named by an identifier that fits more than one Act, because two parliamentary sessions can fall inside one calendar year. We refused to guess between them, so those are recorded as refusals — a refusal, not an absence, and not evidence that nothing refers to them. 36.1% of the OLD preamble parser’s section-level made-under references were wrong — the effects table still holds those, while the enabling rows quoted here came from the fixed parser (measured 14.7 days ago). 41.3% of the instruments sampled had their scheduled text reach our corpus as well — ⚠ a scheduled agreement that was not ingested presents as a SHORT DOCUMENT, not as an error (measured 14.7 days ago). 97,095 act names found in running text resolved to no instrument we hold a title for — short forms that name only a year, and Acts the corpus does not hold. Counted, never dropped (measured 16.1 days ago). Treat any number here as what we found in the layers we have searched, not as a total.
```

⚠⚠ **Never sum the detection kinds, and never present a count as complete.** `enabling` means
the instrument's own enacting words name the power it was made under — the strongest kind, and
the one that may FALL with a repeal. `markup` and `text` mean the source merely refers to the
Act; those survive its repeal. They answer different questions and are listed apart.

⚠ **A provision reference can point at the wrong provision.** 19.1% of non-null
`source_provision_ref` values in the graph point at a provision that does not contain the
reference — Explanatory Notes lead that error. The instrument is reliable; the section number
within it is a lead to check, not a citation to print.

## M-01 — Human Rights Act 1998 and the European Convention on Human Rights

### Provisions — [ukpga/1998/42](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1998/42) · Human Rights Act 1998

**Whose naming:** David's own words (B18 §4).

> he names the Act. "Repeal the Human Rights Act 1998 and denounce the European Convention on Human Rights under Article 58"

**41 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 75 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **368 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (892 references), and **30** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (46 references).

⚠ **226 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 185 of them do not name it.** Those 185 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-02 — Equality Act 2010

### Provisions — [ukpga/2010/15](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/15) · Equality Act 2010

**Whose naming:** David's own words (B18 §4).

> he names the Act. "Repeal the Equality Act 2010, including the public sector equality duty in section 149."

**74 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 148 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **528 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (1552 references), and **97** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (316 references).

⚠ **359 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 285 of them do not name it.** Those 285 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

#### Made under the Act (enabling) — 74 document(s), 148 reference(s)

The instrument's own enacting words name the power it was made under. ⚠ **This is the kind that may fall with a repeal**, and the only kind where that is true. Every enabling row in the graph has a null provision reference by construction — the enacting words sit in the preamble, above any provision — so the blank column here is the shape of the data, not a gap.

### Provisions — [ukpga/2005/4](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2005/4) · Constitutional Reform Act 2005

**Whose naming:** David's own words (B18 §4).

> he names the Act. "Repeal Part 3 of the Constitutional Reform Act 2005"

**120 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 212 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **278 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (840 references), and **42** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (81 references).

⚠ **223 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 103 of them do not name it.** Those 103 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

⚠⚠ **1 confirmed misattribution(s) in this list: `nisr/2010/381`.** Left in and marked, never removed —
a schedule that quietly drops what it knows is wrong cannot be audited.

## M-04 — The arm's-length body estate

### Provisions — [ukpga/2011/24](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2011/24) · Public Bodies Act 2011

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft proposes to amend or use this Act. chosenApproach: "Utilise and extend the Public Bodies Act 2011 to establish a unified accountability framework"; legalLandscape names s.1, s.2, s.12 and Schedules 1–2.

**37 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 51 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **59 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (140 references), and **15** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (22 references).

⚠ **49 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 12 of them do not name it.** Those 12 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-05 — Judicial review of executive decisions

### Provisions — [ukpga/2022/35](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2022/35) · Judicial Review and Courts Act 2022

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft names this Act as the framework it works within; it does not propose to change it. legalLandscape: "The Judicial Review and Courts Act 2022 made modest changes to judicial review"; the draft's own instrument is new, targeted primary legislation defining ouster clauses — a Bill that does not exist yet. Judicial review itself is a common law jurisdiction (B18 §4).

**13 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 22 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **24 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (82 references), and **15** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (35 references).

⚠ **23 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 10 of them do not name it.** Those 10 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-06 — The permanent, appointed civil service

### Provisions — [ukpga/2010/25](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/25) · Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft proposes to amend or use this Act. legalLandscape: "primarily governed by Part 1 of the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010"; the v2 coherent actions open with "Draft and introduce a Government Bill to repeal Part 1 of the Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010". B18 §4 left the 1854-settlement-or-CRAG choice to Charlie; the 1854 settlement is not an enactment, so CRAG is the only linkable candidate.

**16 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 26 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **75 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (149 references), and **15** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (33 references).

⚠ **34 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 18 of them do not name it.** Those 18 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-07 — Operational independence of the Bank of England

### Provisions — [ukpga/1998/11](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1998/11) · Bank of England Act 1998

**Whose naming:** David's own words (B18 §4).

> he names the institution, one founding statute. "Reverse the operational independence of the Bank of England conferred in 1998." The 1998 conferral is the Bank of England Act 1998; he names the year and the effect, and there is exactly one enactment that did it.

**18 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 26 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **217 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (451 references), and **21** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (44 references).

⚠ **190 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 172 of them do not name it.** Those 172 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-08 — Diversity, equity and inclusion practice in the civil service

### Provisions — [ukpga/2010/15](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/15) · Equality Act 2010

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft proposes to amend or use this Act. legalLandscape: "primarily the Equality Act 2010, specifically Section 149"; chosenApproach: "Clarify and narrow the interpretation of the Public Sector Equality Duty (PSED) through official guidance". The same Act as M-02, approached through guidance rather than repeal.

**74 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 148 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **528 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (1552 references), and **97** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (316 references).

⚠ **359 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 285 of them do not name it.** Those 285 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

## M-09 — Gender self-identification

### Provisions — [ukpga/2010/15](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2010/15) · Equality Act 2010

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft proposes to amend or use this Act. chosenApproach: "issue clear, updated guidance under the Equality Act 2010, reflecting the Supreme Court's ruling that 'sex' means biological sex"; the v1 actions open with "Draft an amendment to the Equality Act 2010 to define 'sex' explicitly as biological sex". ⚠ The Gender Recognition Act 2004 is named as framework only and is NOT linked — B18 §4: linking it would assert it provides for self-identification, which it does not.

**74 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 148 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **528 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (1552 references), and **97** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (316 references).

⚠ **359 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 285 of them do not name it.** Those 285 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

**33 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 77 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **337 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (886 references), and **28** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (48 references).

## M-11 — The Sentencing Council and sentencing guidelines

### Provisions — [ukpga/2009/25](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2009/25) · Coroners and Justice Act 2009

**Whose naming:** David's own words (B18 §4).

> he names the institution, one founding statute. "Remove sentencing guidance from an independent council and return it to Parliament or to ministers." The Sentencing Council is created by Part 4 of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009; he names the body, and one enactment constitutes it.

**64 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 115 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **222 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (748 references), and **64** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (165 references).

⚠ **150 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 86 of them do not name it.** Those 86 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

### Provisions — [ukpga/1998/42](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1998/42) · Human Rights Act 1998

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft names this Act as one of the enactments the omnibus would repeal or amend. legalLandscape: "The current legal framework includes the Human Rights Act 1998"

**41 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 75 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **368 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (892 references), and **30** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (46 references).

⚠ **226 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 185 of them do not name it.** Those 185 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

### Provisions — [ukpga/2005/4](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2005/4) · Constitutional Reform Act 2005

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft names this Act as one of the enactments the omnibus would repeal or amend. legalLandscape: "The Constitutional Reform Act 2005 also made significant changes"

**120 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 212 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **278 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (840 references), and **42** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (81 references).

⚠ **223 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 103 of them do not name it.** Those 103 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

⚠⚠ **1 confirmed misattribution(s) in this list: `nisr/2010/381`.** Left in and marked, never removed —
a schedule that quietly drops what it knows is wrong cannot be audited.

### Provisions — [ukpga/2000/36](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2000/36) · Freedom of Information Act 2000

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft names this Act as one of the enactments the omnibus would repeal or amend. legalLandscape names the Freedom of Information Act 2000 among "other key legislation from the 1997-2010 period"

**32 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 54 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **468 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (1149 references), and **43** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (55 references).

⚠ **274 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 242 of them do not name it.** Those 242 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

#### Made under the Act (enabling) — 32 document(s), 54 reference(s)

The instrument's own enacting words name the power it was made under. ⚠ **This is the kind that may fall with a repeal**, and the only kind where that is true. Every enabling row in the graph has a null provision reference by construction — the enacting words sit in the preamble, above any provision — so the blank column here is the shape of the data, not a gap.

### Provisions — [ukpga/1998/46](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1998/46) · Scotland Act 1998

**Whose naming:** the build's drafted kernel — NOT David.

> NAMED BY THE BUILD'S DRAFTED KERNEL, NOT BY DAVID. the draft names this Act as one of the enactments the omnibus would repeal or amend. legalLandscape names the Scotland Act 1998 among the devolution Acts. ⚠ The measure's scope is a DATE RANGE (B18 §4); these four are the ones the draft names, not the list.

**498 instrument(s) identified as made under the Act**, from 1073 enabling reference(s) — one instrument can carry several. A further **1203 document(s)** refer to it from inside a provision (3200 references), and **206** refer to it in a title, long title, preamble or note only (479 references).

⚠ **1093 statutory instrument(s) reference this Act in total; the enacting words of 595 of them do not name it.** Those 595 mention the Act without being made under it, so a repeal does not carry them with it — which is the distinction the count exists to preserve.

⚠⚠ **None of these numbers may be summed, and none is complete.** They are different kinds
of reference with different consequences on repeal; adding them produces a number that
answers no question. The coverage note at the top says which layers were not searched at all.

#### Made under the Act (enabling) — 498 document(s), 1073 reference(s)

The instrument's own enacting words name the power it was made under. ⚠ **This is the kind that may fall with a repeal**, and the only kind where that is true. Every enabling row in the graph has a null provision reference by construction — the enacting words sit in the preamble, above any provision — so the blank column here is the shape of the data, not a gap.
